IF YOU WANT TO BECOME A SENIOR ENGINEER FASTER, STOP COUNTING YEARS.

MEMORIZE THESE 5 LEVERS: 1/5

Own outcomes, not tickets.

Juniors close tasks. Seniors move metrics. Ask what number your work changes. 2/5

Write the doc nobody wants to write.

Design docs, runbooks, postmortems. Visibility compounds faster than commits. 3/5

Delete code on purpose.

Every quarter, kill something: a flag, a service, dead code. Simplifiers get promoted. 4/5

I post daily breakdowns like this for backend, SQL, and interviews.

Follow @owlsky17 so you don't miss the next one. 5/5
THINGS THAT QUIETLY KILL ENGINEERING CAREERS: 1/5

Never asking questions.

Silent confusion ships bugs. The fastest engineers ask the dumb question on day one. 2/5

Avoiding code review feedback.

Defensiveness freezes growth. Treat every comment as free mentoring. 3/5

Staying comfortable one level too long.

If you are the expert in every room, you are in the wrong rooms. 4/5

IF YOU WANT YOUR SIDE PROJECT TO SURVIVE, STOP ADDING FEATURES.

MEMORIZE THESE 5 RULES: 1/5

Ship to one user first.

Yourself counts. Real usage teaches more than ten planned features. 2/5

Boring tech wins weekends.

Monolith, Postgres, one host. Excitement is for work hours. 3/5

Log progress in public.

Weekly demos beat yearly launches. Accountability ships products. 4/5
